title: Reverse group-commit window: commit_delay 100->0, commit_siblings 2->8, wal_writer_flush_after 0->128
configuration_cause: Incumbent carries commit_delay=100us with commit_siblings=2 and wal_writer_flush_after=0. The r010 test (commit_delay 500, siblings 3, flush_after 256) was inconclusive on sync latency and refuted on TPS: the wider window added fixed per-commit stall without coalescing fsyncs (sync_average_ms stayed ~0.10-0.11ms, wal_waiting_backends.max still 1-3). The fixed sleep is pure added latency at 5 terminals; the writer-side flush batching was never actually engaged because flush_after=0 disables it.
mechanism: At 5 terminals the group-commit window cannot collect enough siblings to amortize its fixed sleep, so commit_delay is a pure per-commit tax. Reversing to commit_delay=0 removes the stall; raising commit_siblings to 8 keeps the (now zero) window inactive so no accidental sleep returns. Setting wal_writer_flush_after=128 (1MB) engages background writer flush batching so WAL writes are coalesced on the writer side rather than per-write, reducing wal_waiting_backends queueing without gating foreground commits. This is the opposite direction of the refuted r010 amplitude and targets the writer path, not the commit sleep.
query_effect: InsertTweet commit path loses the fixed 100us sleep; GetUserTweets read path unaffected.
expected_tps_effect: Small increase (0.3-1%) if the commit sleep was a real tax; neutral if WAL sync is already fully amortized.
expected_latency_effect: InsertTweet p95 should drop by the removed sleep; overall p95 roughly unchanged.

predictions.rationale: Removing the 100us fixed commit_delay sleep should lower InsertTweet p95.
Writer-side flush batching at 128 (1MB) should reduce WAL wait queueing versus per-write flushing.
Removing the commit sleep frees terminal capacity for completed transactions.

alternatives.statement: If WAL sync is already fully amortized, removing commit_delay yields no measurable TPS change and the writer flush batching is the only lever.
If the fixed sleep was masking a real fsync bottleneck, removing it raises wal_waiting_backends and sync_average_ms.

why_exceeds_incumbent: Incumbent pays a fixed 100us commit sleep that r010 showed cannot be amortized at 5 terminals, and disables writer flush batching (flush_after=0). Reversing to commit_delay=0 with commit_siblings=8 removes the tax and engages writer-side batching, a direction not yet tested.

nodes.label: Remove fixed commit sleep; engage writer-side flush batching

knob_changes.numerical_basis: Safe low bound 0; r010 showed 500us window refuted sync reduction and inconsistent TPS, so reverse to 0 to eliminate the fixed per-commit stall.
knob_changes.mechanism_role: group-commit collection window; 0 disables the fixed sleep

knob_changes.numerical_basis: Raise from 2 to 8 within safe [0,20]; with 5 terminals, 8 siblings means the (zero) window never activates, preventing accidental stall.
knob_changes.mechanism_role: group-commit activation threshold; high value keeps window inactive

knob_changes.numerical_basis: Set from 0 to 128 (8kB units = 1MB) within safe [0,1024]; engages writer-side flush batching so background writer coalesces WAL writes without gating foreground commits.
knob_changes.mechanism_role: writer flush batch size; batches background WAL writes
